title: City staff named on the boards of their own department’s contractors
question: Which City employees are named as a director, officer or owner of an organization that holds a contract with the department paying their salary?
finding: 15 employee-and-organization pairs with a rare name: the contractor’s list of directors and officers, filed when its contract with a department was approved, carries the name of a person that department was paying in the same fiscal year. 12 are not in the older screens; in 4 of those the organization’s own tax return lists the same name, and the departments paid those 12 organizations $16.7 million in the overlapping years. By department: Public Health 8, Mayor 6, City Administrator 1. A further 25 pairs with common names: counted, not listed.
how: Every director, officer and owner named on a Form 126f4 or 126F contract-approval notice (2018-2026) was matched by first and last name to the City payroll. A pair is kept when the notice’s department contact is the department that paid the person at least $30,000 in the fiscal year of the notice, and the name passes the rarity test used in the people screens. Public bodies, banks, insurers and law firms are left out. The organization’s tax returns and the person’s Form 700 are then read for the same name.
limits: A name on two lists is not one person: every row not confirmed by a Form 700 is a question. Sitting on a nonprofit board is permitted for City staff, many departments encourage it, and some seats are held as part of the job; the conflict rules bite only if the person takes part in the department’s decisions about that organization, which these records do not show. Contractors also file old board lists (see the screen on notices and returns), so a name can outlast the seat. Payments are the department’s to the organization, not to the person.

rows.match: Name match (rare name); second key: the same department (Public Health) in the same years; the organization’s return lists the same name. The records do not show whether this is the same person or two people with the same name; the organization’s board roster with the member’s employer, or the department’s own conflict records, would settle it.
